subject: general
question: Which of the following minerals is found in large quantities in India and holds high economic importance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron ore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Iron ore** is one of the most abundant and economically significant minerals in India, making the country the fourth-largest producer in the world as of 2022.
 
• The majority of iron ore production in India comes from states like Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, and Jharkhand, with Odisha being the largest producer.
 
• India's iron ore is predominantly used in the production of steel, which is critical to the construction, automobile, and infrastructure sectors.
 
• The two main types of iron ore found in India are hematite and magnetite, with hematite being the more dominant type.
 
• India exports significant quantities of iron ore to countries like China and Japan, contributing to its foreign exchange reserves and economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper**

 
 
• Copper is an important metal used in electrical equipment, construction, and industrial machinery due to its excellent conductivity and malleability.
 
• India has limited copper reserves, with key mining areas located in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Jharkhand.
 
• India imports a significant amount of its copper requirements to meet domestic demand.
 
 
 
• **Petroleum**
 
 
• Petroleum is a crucial energy resource and raw material for industries like petrochemicals, plastics, and fertilizers.
 
• India is the third-largest consumer of crude oil globally but relies heavily on imports to meet around 85% of its demand.
 
• Major petroleum-producing regions in India include Assam, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and offshore fields in the Mumbai High basin.
 
 
 
• **Tin**
 
 
• Tin is primarily used in soldering, tin plating, and the production of alloys like bronze.
 
• India has very limited tin reserves, with some deposits found in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, making it dependent on imports to meet domestic demand.
